design.status: exploratory post-hoc extension; selection fixed before scores were inspected
design.causal_contrast: within each comparison only the first name changes; surname, pronouns, qualifications, occupation, template, and query are identical
design.interpretation: sensitivity to Black-associated versus White-associated name strings; not observed candidate race and not a race-only causal effect

name_list.citation: Wilson, Kyra, and Aylin Caliskan. 2024. Gender, Race, and Intersectional Bias in Resume Screening via Language Model Retrieval. AIES 2024.

underlying_perception_database.citation: Elder, Elizabeth Mitchell, and Matthew Hayes. 2023. Signaling Race, Ethnicity, and Gender with Names: Challenges and Recommendations. The Journal of Politics 85(2): 764-770.

sources.surname_rationale: Constant surname Williams, following Wilson and Caliskan (2024): common and approximately balanced between Black and White Census surname categories.

design.selection_rule: Within gender: published racial distinctiveness >= 0.75, equal subword counts under both audited rerankers, then five disjoint pairs minimizing total absolute DOLMA log-frequency distance; male minimum-cost tie broken by larger sum of within-pair minimum distinctiveness.

bootstrap.method: percentile bootstrap; occupations and name pairs resampled independently with replacement; name-pair resampling stratified by gender
